t: What Gravitational Observation Database Is All About
title: What Gravitational Observation Database Is All About
description: Gravity is the weakest force and the hardest to measure: G is known to only 2.2e-5 relative uncertainty. Yet we now hear it: LIGO detected gravitational waves from merging black holes in 2015, squeezing 4-km arms by 1/1000th of a proton's width. From Cavendish's 1798 torsion balance to LIGO's interferometers, each generation measures gravity ten times better. This database is the complete gravitational measurement: full records with definitions, key facts, procedures, and runnable demo programs, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced.

t: Core Vocabulary of Gravitational Observation Database
title: Core Vocabulary of Gravitational Observation Database
description: Every field has its own language. These are the working terms of Gravitational Observation Database — learn them first and every later record reads faster: gravitational wave: ripples in spacetime from accelerating masses; strain: fractional length change from a wave; interferometer: instrument measuring distance via light interference; equivalence principle: gravity accelerates all masses equally.
definition: The working vocabulary of Gravitational Observation Database: the terms practitioners actually use.
key_points: gravitational wave: ripples in spacetime from accelerating masses
strain: fractional length change from a wave
interferometer: instrument measuring distance via light interference
equivalence principle: gravity accelerates all masses equally
redshift: gravity stretching light to longer wavelengths
standard siren: distance measured directly from gravitational waves
